_comment: The one file you tune per project (/harness-init writes the stack bits; harness.schema.json is the field reference). A project = one-or-more components, each with its own gate, plus a cross-cutting root gate.

models._comment: Per-phase {model, fallback, effort, fallbackEffort}: a Claude alias/ID; null = inherit session / no fallback. Fallback fires only on a FAILED invocation (unavailable or usage-limited). Enforced via settings.json `model`, agent frontmatter, and the loop dispatcher — /harness-doctor check 10 validates agreement. `effort` is DECLARED here and ENFORCED by settings.json `effortLevel` (session), the phase agent's `effort:` frontmatter (subagents), and — since 2026-09-04 — `claude --effort` on the headless dispatcher's Claude arm (primary runs at `effort`, a fallback at `fallbackEffort`, else `effort`). Still advisory: fallbackEffort on an INTERACTIVE re-spawn (a usage-cap re-spawn pins the model, not the depth). IDS ARE PINNED, NOT ALIASES: the bare aliases `opus` and `fable` float to the current model of that tier (today Opus 5 / Fable 5.1), so write the full ID for anything whose generation matters. Retuned 2026-09-04 for Claude Fable 5.1 (GA 2026-09-01): session = Fable 5.1 @ medium (Anthropic: medium roughly matches Fable 5 at lower cost, and the orchestrator delegates its deep reasoning); plan/review/evaluate = Fable 5.1 @ high (start at high, raise only on a measured gain); implement stays Opus 5 @ high (Anthropic's own default: start on Opus 5, escalate to Fable only when Opus 5 at higher effort fails). CROSS-VENDOR, since 2026-09-09: Codex was unrouted from 2026-08-11 (single-vendor by decision) until design-doc 002's arm was turned on here — `review.second` is now the Codex CLI, a read-only second judge on the same batch after the primary SHIPs, with SHIP requiring both and no fallback (model diversity is the point; an unreachable second judge fails closed to a human). Its Codex model/depth come from `review.codex`, falling back to the global `models.codex` block below. Every other phase stays Claude. FALLBACKS ONLY ON THE FABLE PHASES (plan/review/evaluate), by decision 2026-08-11: Fable is the model that has actually usage-capped in practice (3x, killing reviews), and a headless run cannot ask a human for help mid-review. implement has NO fallback — if Opus 5 is capped the build simply stops, which is the honest outcome for an interactive phase. DOER != JUDGE: implement is Opus 5 and review is Fable 5.1, so the writer is never the reviewer. Residual edge, accepted knowingly — the review fallback IS Opus 5, so a Fable cap makes the reviewer the same model that wrote the diff. The primary guarantee still holds (the reviewer is a fresh context that never sees the conversation that produced the code); only model diversity is lost, only on a cap, and no diff merges without a human.

codex._comment: GLOBAL Codex CLI defaults, read whenever any phase's model/fallback/second resolves to 'codex'. `model: null` floats on the CLI default deliberately — every *-codex ID was retired in 2026-07/08 and pinned IDs rot (design-doc 002 Consequences); the effective model is read back from the exec transcript header, never assumed. auth/timeoutSeconds are global-only (a per-phase codex block carrying either is a doctor 10(g) error). auth=chatgpt matches this box: `codex login status` reports 'Logged in using ChatGPT' and CODEX_API_KEY is unset (probed 2026-09-09 on codex-cli 0.153.4).

parallel._comment: Fleet runner: opt-in parallel workers over independent tasks (declared 'files' ownership), serialized merge queue. Review bandwidth binds before compute.

gate._comment: This repo's product IS the harness, so its gate is the harness's own self-test twins. `node harness/tests/gate.mjs` is the one spelling the engine can run on both platforms (cmd /c on Windows, bash -lc on Unix) — that script explains why (a bare `bash` under cmd /c is WSL, measured) and dispatches to run-tests.ps1 + run-tests.sh. NOTE for consumer repos: an all-null gate is the shipped-template default; /harness-init fills yours from the real stack.
Cross-cutting gate, run from the repo ROOT after every component gate passes (usually just the e2e; all-null for a single-component project).

promotion._comment: Risk-gated promotion (/promote). Deterministic rules classify the diff first and can only RAISE the tier; a fresh-context risk-classifier agent then runs and can only raise it further. LOW may auto-approve + auto-merge to staging; MEDIUM/HIGH go to a human; anything matching alwaysHuman or moneySignals is HIGH unconditionally; prod is NEVER automated. Off by default — turn on deliberately, per docs/promotion.md.
